Original [BERT4Rec code](https://github.com/FeiSun/BERT4Rec/blob/master/modeling.py) uses learned absolute column positions. Consequently, slicing a length-L endpoint input to its last K columns and rebuilding positions as 0…K−1 shifts every retained token, including MASK, by −(L−K). Preserve original position IDs by slicing them alongside tokens, or keep width L and replace removed history with padding. Nonpadding-count IDs, such as cumsum(valid)−1, ignore left-padding width but renumber retained tokens when actual history is removed; preserving their original values requires computing IDs before cropping. Pure [relative-distance attention](https://aclanthology.org/N18-2074/) preserves retained pairwise distances under a common shift, provided no absolute component or changed distance convention intervenes. These cropping consequences follow from the respective position definitions.

Implementation checks: construct history+[MASK] with space reserved for MASK, then apply identical slicing to tokens, position IDs, labels and supervision masks. Assert retained-token and MASK position IDs match the uncropped reference when testing context removal alone. Read the final nonpadding column—never count−1 for left-padded inputs. Supervise original items at their masked locations; padding and unsupervised locations must have ignored labels. For endpoint prediction, keep the target exclusively in the label, absent from the bidirectional input; [BERT4Rec](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06690) uses masked-item training and appended-MASK inference.

Mask padding keys in every attention layer: [PyTorch MultiheadAttention](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.modules.activation.MultiheadAttention.html) uses key_padding_mask=True to ignore a key. Zero padding embeddings alone cannot block attention after positional embeddings, biases and normalization. Exclude padded query outputs from loss/readout; keep MASK valid to avoid all-masked examples. In evaluation mode, verify padding-content changes leave valid outputs unchanged, and verify predictor-writer preprocessing and position logic match training.
